external_research.source: scikit-learn Common pitfalls and recommended practices
external_research.finding: split before preprocessing; fit/fit_transform only on train; Pipeline is a recommended way to prevent preprocessing leakage.
ColumnTransformer applies different preprocessing by column inside a Pipeline and avoids test-statistic leakage when used correctly.
group-aware evaluation uses non-overlapping groups; a post-hoc overlap counter is not itself a group splitter.
time-ordered validation must preserve ordering; gap/test-size are explicit parts of the split contract.

external_research.source: Feast historical feature retrieval / point-in-time joins
external_research.finding: historical retrieval joins features to an entity dataframe at an event timestamp to enforce point-in-time correctness and avoid future feature values.

external_research.source: Google Rules of Machine Learning / training-serving skew
external_research.finding: same examples at train and serving should produce the same features/results; monitoring only aggregate means is insufficient to prove parity.
pickle/joblib must not load untrusted artifacts and cross-version loading is unsupported/advised against without matching environment metadata.

runtime_counterexamples: catalog_check accepts the same feature name in numeric and categorical simultaneously and still returns catalog_ok=True.
catalog_check treats an absent note as note_len=0 and catalog_ok=True, collapsing missing into empty text.
float('nan') is not marked missing by v is None and propagates NaN through z-score.
graph_feats({}, {}, {}, {}) returns shared_address=1 because None == None.
neighbors={'E1':['E2','E2']} returns degree=2 even though there is one unique neighbor and no declared multiedge semantics.
paths={'E9-E1':1} queried as E1-E9 returns default 99 due directional string key.
window_count(..., w=-1) silently returns 0 instead of rejecting an invalid window.
ModeImputer.fit([None,None,'app']) sets mode=None; transform then raises RuntimeError('not fitted').
ModeImputer.fit([]) raises ValueError from max() rather than a typed fit-state/data-contract error.
ModeImputer tie between ['app','web'] changes winner across PYTHONHASHSEED values because set iteration decides the tie.
time_group_split can return n_test=0, overlap=0 and therefore appear clean despite having no evaluation partition.
Lexicographic timestamp split misclassifies 2026-02-01T00:30:00+01:00 as after 2026-02-01T00:00:00+00:00 although the first instant is chronologically earlier.
leak_scan detects label_decision but misses target, outcome, fraud_result, LabelDecision and post_review.
skew_alert cannot detect distribution changes with equal means, e.g. train [-1,1] vs serve [0,0].

findings.evidence: Roadmap requires S31; continuation marks S31 REPAIR_REQUIRED with broken edge provenance, temporal traversal and graph invariants.
findings.attack: S32 treats S31 graph outputs as usable feature inputs.
findings.defense: S32 uses a tiny synthetic graph fixture rather than claiming it is production truth.
findings.impact: A wrong ER merge or graph edge becomes a learned feature and can contaminate every downstream baseline.
findings.fix: Gate S31 lineage/invariants before graph features; synthetic fixtures must reproduce the repaired contract.

findings.evidence: T2-A graph_feats accepts attrs/neighbors/paths only; no edge_id, graph_version, as_of, etype filter, direction, source or record references.
findings.attack: The resulting degree/path/shared values cannot be reconstructed from evidence.
findings.defense: The prose says features are only topology observed in t.
findings.impact: Feature evidence is unauditable and can inherit future or malformed graph state.
findings.fix: Pass a versioned as-of graph view and persist derivation metadata with each relational feature.

findings.evidence: All eight theory demos end in prints or literal flags; no pytest gate is shown although the roadmap requires systematic pytest from S27.
findings.attack: A broken feature definition can still exit zero.
findings.defense: The snippets are explanatory mini-demos.
findings.impact: The section calls promotion failures gates without executable failure semantics.
findings.fix: Convert each contract to pytest assertions/raises and keep prints only as diagnostics.

findings.evidence: Dictionary carefully calls entity overlap 'contaminación del split' rather than leakage; T4-A later calls the same condition 'leakage de identidad'.
findings.attack: One failure mode receives two meanings inside the same lesson.
findings.defense: Both phrases are commonly used informally.
findings.impact: Learners lose the useful distinction the dictionary itself introduced.
findings.fix: Use 'contaminación por identidad/grupo' consistently; reserve leakage for information unavailable at prediction time/target leakage.

findings.evidence: Prose/outcome promise dtype and missing policy; catalog_check validates only key membership.
findings.attack: A string in a numeric feature can pass catalog_ok=True.
findings.defense: The snippet is labeled minimal.
findings.impact: The catalog is not an executable schema and train/serve type drift can pass the gate.
findings.fix: Represent per-feature dtype, role, missing policy, availability time and validate values before fit/serve.

findings.evidence: set(schema[numeric]+categorical+text) hides duplicate membership; note_len is produced but schema registers raw note instead of the derived feature named in prose.
findings.attack: One feature can belong to two transformation routes and a derived output can exist outside the catalog.
findings.defense: The fixed example has no duplicate keys.
findings.impact: Routing and feature ordering become ambiguous and versioning cannot describe the actual model inputs.
findings.fix: Require disjoint feature groups and register derived feature definitions explicitly.

findings.evidence: catalog_check returns note_len=0 when note is absent.
findings.attack: Missing text and an observed empty string become identical before the missing policy is applied.
findings.defense: Zero length can be a useful feature.
findings.impact: The lesson silently erases a missingness signal it later says must be preserved.
findings.fix: Emit note_missing plus note_len only for observed text, or apply the catalog's explicit missing policy.

findings.evidence: missing_and_scale uses v is None; NaN is treated as observed and propagates into filled/z.
findings.attack: A common tabular missing representation bypasses the gate.
findings.defense: The toy input uses Python None only.
findings.impact: Pandas/NumPy-derived data can carry NaN into model features while silent_fill still prints False.
findings.fix: Use a documented missing predicate covering None/NaN for the supported data types.

findings.evidence: z=(x-mu)/sd has no finite/nonzero sd validation; sd=0 raises ZeroDivisionError.
findings.attack: Constant training features break transform instead of producing a controlled contract result.
findings.defense: The example supplies sd=2.
findings.impact: A routine edge case becomes an untyped runtime failure in serve.
findings.fix: Validate fitted statistics; define constant-feature handling and reject non-finite/invalid state.

findings.evidence: T1-B prints silent_fill=False literally; fill, mu and sd are caller-supplied constants with no fit provenance.
findings.attack: The output claims a property that was not computed.
findings.defense: The comment explains the values are meant to come from train fit.
findings.impact: A learner can mistake a hard-coded assertion for proof that train-only state was used.
findings.fix: Fit the state from an explicit train fixture, persist its provenance and compute the missing-indicator gate from outputs.

findings.evidence: graph_feats computes int(a.get('addr') == b.get('addr')); two absent addresses yield 1.
findings.attack: Missing + missing is converted to a positive shared-address relationship.
findings.defense: The demo passes two observed Av1 values.
findings.impact: The exact false-evidence pattern rejected in S30/S31 reappears as a model feature.
findings.fix: Require both normalized addresses to be observed before shared_address can be 1; otherwise emit missing/unknown.

findings.evidence: graph_feats consumes current neighbors/path tables without feature cutoff or temporal edge filtering.
findings.attack: Edges created after the prediction time can affect degree/path features.
findings.defense: Prose says only topology observed in t should be used.
findings.impact: Graph features can leak future relationships even if transaction windows elsewhere are half-open.
findings.fix: Build graph features from an explicit as_of view with edge event/availability times and frozen graph version.

findings.evidence: degree=len(neighbors[e]); S31 distinguished multigraph incident-edge degree from unique-neighbor count, but T2-A stores only a neighbor list.
findings.attack: Duplicate neighbors can inflate the value, while collapsed multiedges can undercount it.
findings.defense: The paragraph describes degree as two neighbors in this tiny fixture.
findings.impact: The same feature name can change meaning between S31 and S32.
findings.fix: Expose separate incident_edge_count and unique_neighbor_count with graph-view metadata.

findings.evidence: Missing path becomes numeric 99 with no indicator; T1-B says missingness should remain explicit.
findings.attack: Unreachable/unknown is encoded as an extreme observed distance and collides with a legitimate long path.
findings.defense: The prose labels 99 as a default rather than inventing an edge.
findings.impact: The model can interpret absence as ordered numeric evidence.
findings.fix: Return path_exists/path_missing plus path_length when observed, with a bounded/capped representation documented in the catalog.

findings.evidence: Roadmap T2 explicitly requires distance; T2-A heading says 'distancia' but its prose/code implement shared_address, degree and path only.
findings.attack: A named subtopic is not taught or executed.
findings.defense: Graph path length is a type of distance in graph theory.
findings.impact: The learner cannot tell whether roadmap 'distance' means geographic/entity distance or path distance and receives no distance contract.
findings.fix: Name path_length explicitly as graph distance or add the intended geographic/distance feature with units, cutoff and provenance.

findings.evidence: T2-B promises count and frequency by channel; window.py implements only window_count and never computes frequency.
findings.attack: One half of the subtopic/output is absent.
findings.defense: The paragraph explains frequency conceptually.
findings.impact: Outcome 'conteos y frecuencias' is not demonstrated and cannot be regression-tested.
findings.fix: Compute per-channel numerator/denominator from the same half-open eligible events and test support=0.

findings.evidence: window_count counts list entries, not immutable event ids; duplicated/replayed source events count twice.
findings.attack: S31 already found replay inflation in aggregates and S32 inherits it.
findings.defense: The fixture has unique numeric timestamps.
findings.impact: Retry/backfill can inflate transaction counts/frequencies and change model features without new evidence.
findings.fix: Deduplicate by immutable source event identity before window aggregation and retain detail refs.

findings.evidence: Eligibility uses only event ts. It has no recorded_at/ingested_at/available_at field to establish whether the system actually knew the event at decision time.
findings.attack: A late-arriving record with old event_ts can retroactively enter historical training features despite not being available then.
findings.defense: Half-open event-time filtering is already better than using future timestamps.
findings.impact: The key question 'would this value exist at t?' is not satisfied by occurrence time alone.
findings.fix: Define event_time and availability/knowledge_time; historical retrieval must be point-in-time correct on both semantics for the chosen source.

findings.evidence: window_count accepts w<=0; w=-1 silently returns 0.
findings.attack: Invalid configuration looks like a legitimate zero-event feature.
findings.defense: Exercises use positive w.
findings.impact: Configuration errors become data values.
findings.fix: Require finite positive window width and typed/ordered timestamps before counting.

findings.evidence: ModeImputer.fit includes None in max(set(xs), key=xs.count); if None is most frequent, self.mode=None and transform raises 'not fitted'.
findings.attack: A successfully fitted training batch is indistinguishable from an unfitted transformer.
findings.defense: The demonstration train values contain no None.
findings.impact: Exactly the missing-data case this section teaches can break its categorical pipeline.
findings.fix: Exclude missing from mode estimation, store a separate fitted flag and define all-missing behavior.

findings.evidence: Mode ties are broken by set iteration; running ['app','web'] under different PYTHONHASHSEED values selected different modes.
findings.attack: Fitted state can differ between processes for identical data.
findings.defense: The provided fixture has a unique mode.
findings.impact: Violates the deterministic train≡serve/versioning story and makes artifacts irreproducible.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic tie policy (e.g. sorted value or explicit category order) and test it.

findings.evidence: ModeImputer.fit([]) raises ValueError from max().
findings.attack: Empty training slice produces an implementation exception instead of a typed data-contract failure.
findings.defense: A real training split should normally contain rows.
findings.impact: Combined with F31, an empty split can reach fit and fail far from the split gate.
findings.fix: Reject empty/no-observed training input before estimating state.

findings.evidence: column_router takes num_state directly and silently fills numeric None with 0; it has no fitted flag or missing indicator and is outside MiniPipeline state.
findings.attack: The same block that teaches one fitted pipeline introduces a second mutable preprocessing path.
findings.defense: It is presented as a simple ColumnTransformer analogue.
findings.impact: Train and serve can call the router with different arbitrary state and violate the section's core equivalence contract.
findings.fix: Make numeric/categorical/text routes fitted transformers inside one pipeline and carry indicators/state/version through the same object/artifact.

findings.evidence: Roadmap explicitly requires ColumnTransformer and custom transformers; theory executes only a Python analogue and no text route despite T1 text features.
findings.attack: The learner never sees the actual sklearn composition contract required by the roadmap.
findings.defense: The prose intentionally exposes the mechanics without library magic.
findings.impact: The conceptual bridge to S33 sklearn pipelines remains incomplete and text columns are dropped from the routing demonstration.
findings.fix: Keep the pure-Python model, then add a minimal executable Pipeline+ColumnTransformer mapping numeric/categorical/text routes fit only on train.

findings.evidence: load_state is json.loads(json.dumps(state)); no file/artifact is written or read.
findings.attack: An in-memory round-trip is described as persistence and reuse in serve.
findings.defense: The goal is to inspect serialization visibly.
findings.impact: The learner does not demonstrate cross-process/cross-run reuse, the defining property of persisted fit state.
findings.fix: Write/read an actual JSON artifact (or equivalent) with immutable identity/hash and reopen it in a separate serve step/test.

findings.evidence: Prose says state includes mediana, vocab, mu/sigma and schema; demo persists only median and version.
findings.attack: The artifact cannot reproduce the transformations taught in T1/T3.
findings.defense: It is a minimal example focused on the median.
findings.impact: Two runs carrying the same fs-v1 string can implement different vocab/scaling/catalog logic.
findings.fix: Persist complete fitted transformer state plus catalog/schema, missing policy, dependency/code version and derivation metadata.

findings.evidence: version is a caller-provided string; load/apply never validate fs-vN format or bind it to catalog/model/state hash.
findings.attack: A model can be served with incompatible feature state while still printing a plausible version.
findings.defense: The prose tells learners to bump version on change.
findings.impact: Versioning is ceremonial rather than an enforceable compatibility boundary.
findings.fix: Use a manifest with feature_set_id, schema/catalog hash, state hash, transformer/code/dependency versions and expected model binding.

findings.evidence: T3-B says joblib or pickle serve the same production role without warning that loading untrusted pickle/joblib can execute code and cross-version loading is unsupported.
findings.attack: Advanced learners are pointed toward unsafe persistence without the minimum trust boundary.
findings.defense: The course demo itself uses JSON, not pickle.
findings.impact: A later production implementation may deserialize an untrusted or incompatible artifact.
findings.fix: Add a concise trusted-source/version compatibility warning and immutable artifact metadata; retain JSON for inspectable state where possible.

findings.evidence: time_group_split first splits solely by timestamp and only reports entity overlap; it does not create non-overlapping groups.
findings.attack: Calling it a time+group split overstates the algorithm.
findings.defense: Failing when overlap exists is a valid strict gate for a fixed cutoff.
findings.impact: Real data with entities on both sides cannot be split by the taught function; the learner has no method to produce a valid group-aware holdout.
findings.fix: Define the evaluation estimand, then implement group-disjoint holdout/GroupKFold or a custom chronological group split and report exclusions.

findings.evidence: Rows compare r['ts'] < cut as strings. With timezone offsets, lexicographic order can disagree with chronological order.
findings.attack: A chronologically pre-cutoff event can enter test or vice versa.
findings.defense: The toy fixture uses zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD strings.
findings.impact: Temporal leakage gate is only correct for a narrow undocumented timestamp representation.
findings.fix: Parse/validate timezone-aware datetimes and compare normalized instants; reject malformed/naive values per contract.

findings.evidence: Function can return n_train>0, n_test=0, overlap=0; current demo's ok tests only overlap.
findings.attack: A split with no holdout can look valid.
findings.defense: The provided fixture has one row each side.
findings.impact: S33 could train without an evaluable test set while the S32 gate reports zero overlap.
findings.fix: Require minimum support for train/test/groups and report support before promotion.

findings.evidence: leak_scan only tests case-sensitive substrings 'label'/'decision'; counterexamples target, outcome, fraud_result, LabelDecision and post_review pass.
findings.attack: Feature names are not a reliable oracle for target/post-outcome availability.
findings.defense: The prose calls them red flags, not a complete semantic proof.
findings.impact: The later gate promotes based on an incomplete scanner and can miss obvious response-derived features.
findings.fix: Give every feature catalog metadata for role, source, availability/knowledge time and derivation; name scanning remains a secondary heuristic.

findings.evidence: skew_alert compares only aggregate means. Different distributions or per-row feature mismatches can have identical means.
findings.attack: Mean equality can coexist with broken train/serve feature logic.
findings.defense: The paragraph presents mean difference as an example simple alert.
findings.impact: The core train≡serve gate is not tested; errors can cancel in aggregate.
findings.fix: Replay the same raw examples through train/serve transformation and compare feature vectors/schema exactly, then add distribution monitoring separately.

findings.evidence: One absolute tol=0.5 is used on means without feature units/scale/support.
findings.attack: 0.5 can be huge for one feature and negligible for another.
findings.defense: The value is an illustrative toy threshold.
findings.impact: Learners may copy an unscaled threshold as a generic monitoring rule.
findings.fix: Label it explicitly illustrative and define feature-specific normalized/statistical tolerances with support/window metadata.

findings.evidence: leakage.py prints leaky=['label_decision'], skew=True and feature_set='fs-v2' but never computes/rejects promotion.
findings.attack: The output shows a versioned feature set in the same run that should be blocked.
findings.defense: The prose says promotion is allowed only when checks are clean.
findings.impact: A learner sees diagnostics rather than an actual blocking gate, repeating the false-green pattern from S27-S31.
findings.fix: Implement promote_status/exception requiring semantic leakage checks, parity checks and valid manifest before returning a promoted id.

findings.evidence: T4-B callout maps both leaky features and skew to REJECT_LEAKAGE although the dictionary teaches them as different failure classes.
findings.attack: Root cause is lost in gate status.
findings.defense: Both conditions should block promotion.
findings.impact: Operators cannot distinguish response/future leakage from train-serving mismatch and choose the correct repair.
findings.fix: Use distinct REJECT_LEAKAGE and REJECT_TRAIN_SERVE_SKEW while both block promotion.

findings.evidence: Dense code-switching includes feature catalog, dtype, row, keys, fill, z-score, vocab, one-hot, Pipeline, ColumnTransformer, custom transformer, joblib, pickle, group split, tol and CI; several are used before a concrete Spanish-first definition.
findings.attack: A ZERO_TECH learner must supply tooling vocabulary not always earned in the immediate paragraph.
findings.defense: S32 is advanced and the dictionary explains leakage/train/serve/half-open/skew/fs-vN.
findings.impact: The conceptual difficulty of leakage is compounded by avoidable terminology decoding.
findings.fix: Introduce Spanish concept first and API/English token second, especially dtype, one-hot, router/ColumnTransformer, serialization and group split.

rejected_findings.claim: Every imputation without a missing indicator is universally invalid.
rejected_findings.reason: Adding an indicator can be useful and is a deliberate PyArcana policy here, but it is not a universal statistical law. The defect is in the code's silent/miscomputed missingness, not the mere existence of an imputer.

rejected_findings.claim: A half-open [t-w,t) window is inherently wrong because an event at exactly t might be known.
rejected_findings.reason: The lesson explicitly defines t as its decision cutoff and chooses a conservative half-open contract. That convention is defensible when applied consistently; availability-time provenance remains the real gap.

rejected_findings.claim: Using a pure-Python pipeline analogue is pedagogically invalid.
rejected_findings.reason: The analogue is useful for mechanism visibility. The confirmed issue is roadmap incompleteness: S32 never follows it with the actual ColumnTransformer/Pipeline contract it promises.

rejected_findings.claim: Mean shift is never useful for monitoring.
rejected_findings.reason: Mean difference is a valid lightweight signal. It is insufficient as the sole proof of train≡serve parity and can miss shape/per-row mismatches.
They are legitimate for trusted, version-controlled Python artifacts. The defect is omitting the trust and compatibility warning.

rejected_findings.claim: Current live card definitely contradicts the source's 9-hour estimate.
rejected_findings.reason: The public text index is about four weeks old; it shows the previous 10–18h tagline while canonical main now says about 9h. A fresh rendered fetch is required before treating deployment drift as material.

priority_order: 1. Prevent false relational evidence/future leakage: F01,F02,F11,F12,F13,F14,F17,F18.
3. Make feature catalog/version artifacts real: F05,F06,F07,F25,F26,F27.

USABLE: Fit statistics/vocabulary on train and transform train/test/serve with frozen state.
Half-open feature windows are a defensible explicit decision-time policy.
Target/post-outcome columns must not become model inputs.
Train-serving skew is distinct from offline preprocessing leakage.
Missingness should remain explicit under the course's feature policy.
Relational/graph features are structural signals, not fraud/kinship verdicts.
Feature-set versioning is the correct abstraction boundary toward S33.
PARTIAL: Executable feature catalog with dtype/missing/role/availability metadata.
As-of graph feature retrieval with provenance.
Exact train-serve parity testing and promotion gate.
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: catalog_ok means dtype/missing policy are valid
absent text is equivalent to empty text
None is the only missing representation
current graph topology is safe for historical features
path missing can safely be encoded as observed value 99 without indicator
event_time alone proves the record was known at decision time
a post-hoc overlap counter is a group split
lexicographic timestamp order is chronological order
feature names containing label/decision are a complete leakage detector
an fs-vN string proves state/model compatibility
joblib/pickle are safe regardless of artifact provenance
